rv.q: The simulated instrumentation is extraordinary: not only do the performers recreate booming bass lines and pounding kick drums, they also mimic-pluck violins and jazzy, brushed-snare shuffles.
Funny, inventive, and occasionally moving, Birmingham Rep’s actor-musician production reimagines the classic tale through a distinctly modern lens while retaining its essential heart.
Peter Pan is a spirited family adventure which, true to its Victorian roots, chooses to put the strength of the performances above the use of gaudy special effects.

‘Goodbye Make Believe’ offers a lovely insight into her character and is a particular highlight of Act One. Meanwhile, Iverson Yabut captures the naivety and stubbornness of Peter Pan, and there is an interesting contrast between his determination to remain a child forever and Wendy’s evolving understanding of what growing up might mean.
It is a wonderful alternative to a traditional pantomime and well worth taking your child to see over the festive period.
Despite the doubling, both my granddaughters managed to keep up and enjoy the show.
Ultimately, this Peter Pan is more successful at reinventing how Neverland sounds than at communicating the story that unfolds within it.

cn.t: Critics are largely won over by this hip-hop, beatbox reimagining of Barrie's classic at Polka Theatre. The all-vocal live soundscape earns particular praise, though execution is uneven.
